title: Physics: Electricity & Magnetism
description: Electric fields, circuits, magnetic forces, and induction as foundations for instrumentation, stimulation, sensing, and electrochemical biology.

outcomes.description: Use field and potential models for charge distributions.
Relate circuit measurements to sensor loading and safety limits.

lesson_objectives.description: Connect electric field to force and potential difference.
Use capacitor geometry and energy relations.
Apply Kirchhoff's laws to lumped circuits.
Predict exponential charging or discharging behavior.
Use the right-hand rule for magnetic forces.
Apply Faraday's law to changing magnetic flux.
Interpret impedance as frequency-dependent opposition to current.
Distinguish electrode polarization from tissue signal.
Calculate a cell's membrane capacitance from specific capacitance and area, and relate it to the dielectric constant and thickness with C = εA/d.
Compute the charge and number of ions needed to change membrane potential and compare it with the ions present in the cell.
Calculate the electric field across the membrane and the membrane RC time constant, and interpret both.

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

lessons.title: Electric fields, potential, and capacitance
lessons.worked_example: A 2 μF capacitor at 5 V stores U=½CV²=25 μJ.

lessons.title: Current, resistance, and RC transients
lessons.worked_example: For R=100 kΩ and C=10 μF, τ=RC=1 s; after one time constant a charging capacitor reaches about 63% of its final value.

lessons.title: Magnetic forces and induction
lessons.worked_example: A coil's flux changes from 0 to 0.02 Wb in 0.01 s. One turn has induced emf magnitude |ΔΦ/Δt|=2 V.

lessons.title: Electrodes, impedance, and measurement
lessons.worked_example: A 1 MΩ sensor source connected to a 1 MΩ input forms a divider and loses half its voltage; a 100 MΩ input reduces this loading substantially.

lessons.title: The cell membrane as a capacitor: charge, ions, fields and the membrane time constant
lessons.worked_example: A 10 μm sphere has 12.6 pF; a 100 mV swing moves 1.26×10⁻¹² C, about 7.8×10⁶ ions, roughly 2×10⁻⁵ of its potassium; the field at 70 mV is 1.4×10⁷ V/m and τ = 10 ms.
